messages:
mike_sales: FYI inbound from FinTrust (CISO + infra lead). They want consolidated telemetry for Redwood usage inside their app. Key asks:
- per-tenant cost breakdown by model + route
- per-route latency (p50/p95) and simple histograms
- trace link mapping: Redwood request_id -> their Sentry/Apm URL
- daily export to Snowflake (or S3) and 90d retention
- webhook for anomaly alerts (thresholds on cost/latency)
They want a pilot on Hosted within ~4 weeks. Attaching the email and a few sample request ids below.

mike_sales: ```sample_request_ids:
req_20260318_01a2b3c4
req_20260318_01a2b3c5
req_20260318_01a2b3c6```

sanjay_p: Thanks — can you paste the customer email here and confirm hosted vs dedicated? Also any legal/NDA constraints?

mike_sales: Pasted email in thread. Pilot must be on Hosted initially; they said they may move to Dedicated later. FinTrust is okay signing an NDA for limited access. They can provide S3 credentials or Snowflake target for export.

toni_support: We already have tenant-level billing exports, but we don't currently split cost by route. Per-route cost needs token-level attribution (route tag on each request) + a cost model to attribute infra + model cost. Also exposing request_id in logs with a clickable trace_url is straightforward if eng-runtime adds the field to the request envelope.

laura_pd: Quick scoping suggestion for an MVP (to keep pilot realistic within 4 weeks):
1) Surface per-route latency metrics (p50/p95) in the console for a single customer/tenant.
2) Add a daily aggregated export (S3 CSV / Snowflake-ready) with: date, tenant_id, route, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, infer_cost_usd (estimated), infra_share_usd.
3) Add request-level trace_url field in logs so support/customer can click through to their Sentry (we store the mapping template).
4) Prototype webhook for anomaly alerts (budget spike / latency regression) with basic thresholds.
90d retention: pipeline/storage needs product+infra signoff; for pilot we can store aggregates for 90d, raw logs for 14d.

opsbot: Created backlog issue INFR-3218 and a customer intake card: https://app.prod/issues/INFR-3218 :white_check_mark:

sanjay_p: Good. FinTrust already agreed to limited-scope pilot (single tenant, hosted). They'll provide S3 or Snowflake creds and a list of sample request_ids and their Sentry URL pattern. I can set up a Monday kickoff 30m call.

mike_sales: Confirmed — they said single-tenant pilot is fine. NDA in flight. They prefer CSV export to their S3 bucket for the first iteration.

toni_support: A few open questions from support side: how do we compute 'infra_share_usd' per route? Do we use model runtime + GPU-hours attribution or an averaged per-token multiplier? We need finance to sign off on the computation method before we ship exported cost numbers.

laura_pd: Proposed launch criteria for pilot (product + compliance + finance):
- per-route daily cost aggregate available and matches billing within 5% for sample days
- trace links resolve to customer's Sentry for sampled requests
- export to customer's S3/Snowflake completes successfully and is accessible to their engineers
- console view for p50/p95 by route + simple drilldown to sample traces
- security checklist completed (no PII in exported payloads, access controls validated)
If we meet these, we can widen pilot. Owners: sanjay -> PM lead, toni -> support lead, eng-runtime (add trace_url) and eng-platform (export pipeline) TBD.

sanjay_p: I'll schedule the kickoff and include eng-runtime, platform, and finance. Monday 10am PT works for me. Who from infra should we pull in?

toni_support: :hand: I'll join and bring the support-runbook draft. Also request eng-runtime to estimate effort for adding trace_url and route tagging.

laura_pd: OK. I'll open the product spec PR after the kickoff with the proposed MVP scope and acceptance criteria. We should aim for a canary limited to FinTrust only to reduce blast radius.

mike_sales: Thanks everyone. I'll send the calendar invite and paste the customer's S3 details into the intake card after NDA.
